Purdue Global subscriptions: ExcelTrack costs and the closed $195 enrollment option

Purdue Global’s $195-per-month independent Professional Studies option closed to new enrollments and reentries on July 1, 2026. New students considering a subscription degree should compare an available program such as ExcelTrack using its own tuition, credit units and completion requirements.

The two prices describe different programs

The current 2026–27 Professional Studies catalog states that the independent program is closed to new enrollments and reentries effective July 1, 2026. Its continuing appearance on a tuition page is not evidence that a new student can enroll. Eligible continuing students should confirm which catalog and billing model govern their enrollment.

ExcelTrack Business Administration is a separate bachelor’s program using term-based competency study. Its advertised flat tuition does not inherit the Professional Studies monthly price. Purdue Global is institutionally accredited by the Higher Learning Commission; accreditation does not establish that the two programs have interchangeable admission, curriculum, funding or assessment rules.

Budget ExcelTrack by ten-week term

Purdue Global’s current tuition schedule lists ExcelTrack Business Administration at $2,500 tuition plus a $345 resource fee per term, or $2,845 in those published charges. The university’s business program listing identifies ten-week terms. One, two and three paid terms therefore produce $2,845, $5,690 and $8,535 in this tuition-and-resource-fee scenario.

These figures assume the listed rate remains applicable and include only the stated tuition and resource fee. They exclude any other applicable charges, outside coursework and financial aid. They are not promised degree totals. Completing more approved work in a paid term can improve the effective price per completed requirement, but study time, feedback, prerequisites and the remaining curriculum determine whether that pace is realistic.

Different billing models; the legacy monthly model is not open to new enrollments or reentries.
Program/modelPublished chargePlanning consequence
ExcelTrack BSBA$2,500 tuition + $345 resource fee per ten-week term$2,845 per paid term before other applicable charges and aid
Independent Professional Studies, eligible continuing students only$195 per month + $100 per assessment + $2,226 PR499 capstoneMonthly tuition continues during the capstone; assess remaining assessments separately

Keep quarter credits distinct from semester credits

The ExcelTrack BSBA requires 180 quarter credits. Purdue’s program page describes 174 single-credit competency courses plus a six-quarter-credit capstone. These are quarter credits, so the 180 figure should not be compared as though it were a 180-semester-credit degree.

Purdue’s prior-learning policy permits externally assessed prior learning for no more than 75% of an undergraduate credential. Applied to a 180-quarter-credit bachelor’s, that gives a mathematical ceiling of 135 quarter credits and leaves at least 45 outside that external-credit ceiling. It does not establish that 135 quarter credits will fit your BSBA.

The capstone is excluded from credit for prior learning. Equivalent learning, documentation, minimum results and actual degree applicability still need review. Do not describe all remaining credits as conventional classroom courses: Purdue also has internal assessment mechanisms with their own residency treatment. Ask for the individual remaining-work evaluation rather than building a plan from the percentage alone.

The capstone still needs its own calendar

Purdue describes the ExcelTrack BSBA capstone as a traditional six-quarter-credit course charged at the ExcelTrack tuition rate. A competency-based structure therefore does not mean every requirement is an independently accelerated one-credit unit. Confirm the capstone’s timing, prerequisites and course expectations when estimating the number of paid terms.

This research did not establish a program-wide guarantee of non-proctored assessments. Ask about the actual remaining courses and technical requirements if assessment format affects your decision. The tuition page also describes funding restrictions that are specific to ExcelTrack, including exclusions for certain VA and federal tuition-assistance benefits; resolve the applicable funding before enrolling.

For continuing Professional Studies students, include every charge

The published independent Professional Studies model combines $195 monthly tuition, $100 per assessment and a separate $2,226 PR499 capstone charge. Monthly tuition is additional to the capstone amount. Four professional-competency tutorials and assessment-attempt rules also belong in the remaining-work plan; paying an assessment fee is not an award of credit.

A purely illustrative budget with three paid months, four paid assessments and one capstone would be 3 × $195 + 4 × $100 + $2,226 = $3,211 before any other applicable charges or aid. Those are selected inputs, not a prediction that the degree or capstone can be completed in three months. Substitute the actual months and assessments from your continuing-student evaluation.

A continuing student should ask which existing credits apply, which assessments remain, whether any reentry would be barred by the closure, and what happens if a pause extends the schedule. Preserve existing records and catalog terms; the July 2026 admission closure is not evidence that valid earlier coursework disappears.

Compare the work left before choosing the monthly or term headline

For a new applicant, start with programs currently accepting students. For an eligible continuing student, start with the approved remaining requirements and applicable catalog. In either case, keep outside-credit costs, assessment charges, capstone charges and university billing periods in separate rows.

Then run a slower-pace scenario as well as your hoped-for one. Another ExcelTrack term adds the listed term charge; another eligible legacy monthly period adds its monthly tuition. An inexpensive advertised starting rate is useful only when it belongs to an available program and fits the work you actually have left.
